name: Live in Chicago
description: Released in 1990 to support the 1989 Neon Hearts tour.
subtitle: The 1990 Tour EP (Recorded Before "The Crash")
linerNotes: Recorded at The Midwest Horizon Arena (commonly called Midwest Horizon) in Chicago as the opening act on the Neon Hearts tour, just weeks before the December 10, 1990 accident on I-81 that changed everything. To this day, the band openly hates this album—and only keeps it in the public catalog for strict historical and legal record-keeping (specifically because Ryan's spoken introduction on Track 1, "And this is my sister, Cassidy!", served as the courtroom smoking gun in 1992 proving Apex Records' executives never bothered to listen to their own tapes).

Even though the headliners on the tour were close family friends who wanted The Stardust Engine to come back out and jam with them at the end of the night, Apex Records executives said "Absolutely not," locking the band inside a strict 30-minute support-slot box and sabotaging the Front-of-House mix by burying Cassidy's signature "Stardust" synthesizer leitmotif. Beneath the ruined mix, you can hear Evan and Tyler playing 15 BPM faster in sheer fury, Ryan physically anchoring Cassidy on stage after Track 4 triggered a mid-set breakdown, and a band trying to tear its way out of a corporate cage.

studioArchives.title: Historical Context
studioArchives.content: This is the last official recording of Ryan O'Connell performing standing up. Later that year, on the night of December 10, 1990 on Interstate 81 Northbound at Mile Marker 98 (Exit 98, Newbern, Virginia), the band's 1988 Holt Freighter touring van was clipped on black ice.

studioArchives.title: The 30-Minute Opening-Act Box
studioArchives.content: Why was The Stardust Engine playing an 18,000-seat arena like Midwest Horizon in 1989–1990? Because they were the opening act for headliners who happened to be close family friends. The headliners wanted Ryan and Cassidy to come back out during the main set to jam with them, but Apex Records executives flatly forbade it ("Absolutely not—stay in your thirty-minute box"). Twelve years later at The Chancellery in 2002, when opening act Crimson Node joined The Stardust Engine on stage for an eleven-minute jam on "The Flight Path," Ryan finally righted that wrong.

link.label: Listen to "The Flight Path (Live at the Chancellery)"

studioArchives.title: The Despised "Mall-Pop" Cover & The Aborted 1991 Shopping Mall Tour
studioArchives.content: Why does the cover of Live in Chicago look like a hand-airbrushed pastel teen-romance poster where Ryan and Cassidy look like husband and wife singing a love ballad while Evan and Tyler are reduced to faceless silhouettes in pink fog? Because Apex Records' L.A. marketing department forced that cover onto the band as a test balloon to pitch them for a Spring 1991 Regional Shopping Mall Atrium Tour—wanting four CPI graduates in their twenties to mime over DAT backing tapes next to suburban food-court escalators. On the night of December 10, 1990, Ryan was sitting in the front lounge marking up Apex's shopping-mall tour itinerary with a red pen when the bus hit black ice at Mile Marker 98, killing the mall tour forever.

studioArchives.title: The "Engine" Awakens
studioArchives.content: Listen closely to Evan and Tyler's rhythm section on this record. Stripped of the studio click-track, they play the songs 15 BPM faster and infinitely heavier than the album versions, foreshadowing the hard rock sound of their 1995 independent rebirth.

liveTranscript.title: The Anchor On Stage: Live Transcript
liveTranscript.venue: The Midwest Horizon Arena (Midwest Horizon), Chicago, IL (1990)
paragraphs: Midway through the thirty-minute opening set, singing "If You Walked Away" (Track 4) triggers a visceral wave of abandonment terror in Cassidy. With the Apex tour manager standing in the wings tapping his watch, there is no time to stop—she has to survive "Light Up the Night" (Track 5) on sheer autistic masking and muscle memory while 18,000 teenagers roar in the dark.

As the final synth chord of "Light Up the Night" fades, Ryan looks across the stage and sees his sister's hands trembling on her keyboard tier. Ignoring the label's script, Ryan walks straight over to Cassidy's riser, plants himself right beside her, and speaks into his microphone before playing the entire guitar solo of "My Anchor Holds" pressed back-to-back against his sister to ground her through the end of the set:
liveTranscript.quote: This is a song for that one person who keeps you sane... the one who's your anchor.
liveTranscript.attribution: Ryan O'Connell, grounding Cassidy on stage before "My Anchor Holds" (Track 6)
